minutes.headline: Personnel Committee reviewed counsel's proposed SAP changes without voting on them, and approved a meal site manager at a higher grade and a new assistant position.
minutes.summary: Labor counsel walked the committee through his recommended revisions to the Salary Administration Plan. The discussion covered the grievance and appeal language, Juneteenth in exchange for personal time, vacation accrual, promotion placement, layoff seniority, overtime wording and minimum wage. No SAP changes were voted. The committee then approved the meal site manager job description at a higher grade and the new assistant meal site manager position. It set the next meeting for the following Monday.

public_comment.topic: A speaker thanked the committee for letting SAP employees speak, asked whether a meeting date would be set, and said she wants to hear from SAP employees.
Public comment was nearly skipped; the chair said it would be made a regular agenda item going forward.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of December 13th 2021, noting Donna was absent.
votes.outcome: passed; members voted aye by roll call, Donna abstained

votes.motion: Increase the meal site manager grade from the recommended grade five to grade six.
votes.outcome: passed; roll call of ayes heard

votes.motion: Approve the meal site manager job description as amended.
votes.outcome: passed; roll call of ayes heard

votes.motion: Approve the assistant meal site manager position.
votes.outcome: passed; roll call of ayes heard

budget_items.topic: Meal site manager and assistant positions
budget_items.what_was_said: The new roles would be budgeted in the fiscal 23 budget and coincide with the new pay rates in July. Compensation is below some comparable towns.
Members compared grade five, six and eight rates and settled on grade six. The assistant stays at the current grade and step.

budget_items.topic: Minimum wage in the salary grid
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the lowest grades fall below state minimum wage and the FY23 grid should start at the state minimum, which was said to be rising to the next level.
A new salary grid is needed by the warrant deadline for annual town meeting. Julie is polling comparable towns for wages.
Members recalled a fixed percentage between steps and grades that should be preserved if grades are reduced.

decisions.decision: Members will send concerns on counsel's recommendations to Julie, who will compile them for the next meeting. Uncontroversial changes may be taken together by consent.
Next meeting set for Monday the 31st at 5 p.m. by Zoom, to cover two new SAP positions, a new hire above step one, and a first pass at the SAP changes.
Public comment will be a standing agenda item.
Counsel will review the vacation receive-versus-accrue wording, draft alternative layoff language and clean up the promotion example.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee approved a higher pay grade for a new meal site manager job than counsel had recommended.
The committee approved the meal site manager job description as amended.
The committee approved a new assistant meal site manager position.
Labor counsel walked through proposed Salary Administration Plan changes; none were voted, and counsel will revise the vacation, layoff and promotion language.
The next meeting is set for Monday the 31st at 5 p.m. by Zoom, and public comment becomes a standing agenda item.

why_it_matters: The two new meal site positions would be budgeted in the fiscal 23 budget starting in July, so residents may be asked to fund them at town meeting.

The Salary Administration Plan rules on grievances, holidays, vacation, layoffs and the pay grid for town employees are still unsettled, and a new salary grid is needed by the warrant deadline for annual town meeting.
